record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.original_question: Is there a clear structural account of how the additional degrees that appear in the extended Weihrauch degrees are related to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees?

evidence.quote: Open Question 19. Is there a clear picture of how the additional degrees in the extended Weihrauch degrees relate to the Weihrauch degrees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A multi-valued function (problem) on Baire space is a partial relation $f \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}} \times \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, where the domain consists of "instances" and, for each instance $x$, the set $f(x) = \{y : (x,y) \in f\}$ is the set of "solutions". Weihrauch reducibility $f \le_W g$ holds iff there exist computable functionals $H, K$ such that, for every instance $x$ of $f$, $K(x)$ is an instance of $g$ and, for every solution $y$ of $g$ on $K(x)$, $H(x,y)$ is a solution of $f$ on $x$. The resulting equivalence classes form the Weihrauch degrees, a lattice studied in computable analysis.

Extended Weihrauch reducibility generalises this notion by allowing the "instances" and "solutions" to be arbitrary subsets of Baire space (rather than single points), and by formulating the reduction in a realizability framework (e.g. as instance degrees in the Kleene–Vesley realizability topos). The resulting structure, the extended Weihrauch degrees, contains a canonical embedding of the ordinary Weihrauch degrees but properly extends them with additional degrees not arising from any single multi-valued function in the classical sense.

Problem. Provide a clear structural account describing how the additional degrees that occur in the extended Weihrauch degrees but not in the (image of the) ordinary Weihrauch degrees relate to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees. In particular, characterise the new degrees in terms of natural operations (such as suprema, infima, implications, or other lattice-theoretic / topos-theoretic constructions) applied to ordinary Weihrauch degrees, or otherwise describe their position within the extended Weihrauch lattice relative to the embedded copy of the ordinary Weihrauch degrees.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has clarified part of the picture: the ordinary Weihrauch degrees embed into the extended Weihrauch degrees as the ¬¬-dense modest instance degrees in a (relative) realizability topos, and a topos-theoretic semantics for the extended degrees has been developed. This provides a structural framework relating the two, but a fully explicit characterisation of all "new" extended degrees in terms of operations on ordinary Weihrauch degrees does not appear to be completely settled, so the question is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A topos for extended Weihrauch degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Extended Weihrauch degrees are formulated through instance degrees in a relative realizability topos; ordinary Weihrauch reducibility coincides with extended Weihrauch reducibility on the ¬¬-dense modest predicates.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a topos-theoretic account embedding ordinary Weihrauch degrees into the extended Weihrauch degrees and characterising them as ¬¬-dense modest instance degrees.

status_evidence.title: Instance reducibility and Weihrauch degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces instance reducibility and relates the resulting extended Weihrauch structure (with computable infima, suprema, and implication) to ordinary Weihrauch degrees.
status_evidence.claim: Frames the extended Weihrauch degrees as instance degrees with additional lattice-theoretic structure containing the ordinary Weihrauch degrees.
